items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: And then one day I heard this Art Tatum thing, and it was like suddenly getting a focus. I felt, you know, if I could play like that, you know. And I spent the last 50 years trying

ctx.x: It’s interesting to talk, we have talked with I think one other person who came from England — Jillean Williams actually — and we were getting her take on how jazz was kind of spread from America to other parts, and we wondered if you could tell us how it came to be that you became a jazz musician.

Well, it was disseminated through records of course, and when I was a kid, you couldn’t buy American records for some — I’ll never understand to this day why — but they weren’t allowed. The government after the war distrusted everybody I think and American records were not allowed in. But somehow I got to hear a record by Art Tatum, it’s an absolute classic, “Tea for Two.” And up until then I’d just been listening to everybody and imitating anybody, any piano player. I mean I didn’t know the difference between a…
a focus. I felt, you know, if I could play like that, you know. And I spent the last 50 years trying, never succeeded, but—
